issues.legal_issue: The use of potentially lethal force to protect disputed land was not justified as an exercise of the right of private defence on the evidence presented.
material_facts: Revenue records named the accused side, but the entries were contested and proceedings concerning them were pending.
The opposing group claimed possession, and evidence accepted by the High Court rebutted the presumption arising from the revenue entries.
The High Court found no evidence that the opposing group was armed with firearms or had fired first; the items said to be empty cartridges were found to be plastic pieces.
No member of the accused group had sustained an injury.
The accused used weapons capable of causing death, and the Supreme Court found no error in the High Court’s assessment of the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The appellants’ claim of private defence was rejected, and the convictions and sentences upheld by the High Court were affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 117 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1939, a revenue entry gives rise to a rebuttable presumption of possession, which may be displaced by evidence. Even assuming a person is in possession of land, that fact does not justify using firearms or other weapons capable of causing death merely against persons attempting to trespass. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by convicted persons challenging their convictions.
predicates.deadly_force_used_to_protect_land: The accused used firearms or other weapons capable of causing death in an incident connected with protecting land.
predicates.opponents_not_proved_armed_or_to_have_fi: The evidence did not establish that the opposing group was armed with lethal weapons or fired first.

issues.definition: When convicted persons appeal and the evidence does not establish that the opposing group was armed or fired first, using potentially lethal force to protect land results in rejection of the private-defence claim and affirmance of the conviction.
